title: Auracast Explained: One Audio Broadcast, Many Listeners
headline:
One screen.
Many sets of earbuds.
meaning: Auracast broadcasts audio to compatible receivers.
example: Listeners can join a nearby supported broadcast.
comparison: Broadcast audio differs from one-to-one pairing.
caution: Both transmitter and receiver need support.
question: Where would shared audio be useful?
lines: Imagine several people listening to the same television through their own earbuds. Auracast is designed for shared audio.
A compatible transmitter broadcasts an audio stream that nearby compatible receivers can join.
Instead of creating a separate one to one link for every listener, one broadcast serves many receivers.
A phone or another assistant can help you discover the broadcast and choose which stream to hear.
An ordinary Bluetooth label alone is not enough. Check Auracast support on both ends of the connection.
